cities.name: Mykonos
cities.summary: Mykonos pairs Cycladic lanes and beach clubs with easy ferry access to one of Greece's great ancient sites. It is compact, photogenic and geared to sun, dining and nightlife.

cities.name: Thessaloniki
cities.summary: Greece's second city mixes Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman layers with a lively seafront and food scene. It is one of the country's best urban breaks for history, markets and nightlife.

cities.name: Meteora
cities.summary: Meteora's monasteries rise from sheer sandstone pillars in one of Europe's most dramatic landscapes. Come for the viewpoints, trails and extraordinary religious heritage.

clusters.name: Kastraki Trails
attractions: Byzantine Church of the Dormition of the Virgin Mary

cities.name: Delphi
cities.summary: Delphi sits high on Mount Parnassus above Greece's most evocative oracle sanctuary. It is a compact stop for classical ruins, mountain air and sweeping valley views.

cities.name: Corfu
cities.summary: Corfu combines Venetian townscapes, green hills and easy swimming coves. The island works well for a longer stay thanks to its heritage core, beaches and scenic drives.

cities.name: Zakynthos
cities.summary: Zakynthos is known for bright turquoise water, boat trips and dramatic limestone scenery. It suits beach time, marine-life outings and short scenic drives around the island.

cities.name: Crete
cities.summary: Crete is a full-scale destination with Minoan sites, superb food, long beaches and varied mountain landscapes. It rewards road-trippers and slow stays far beyond a quick island stop.

cities.name: Madrid
cities.summary: Madrid delivers grand boulevards, world-class art and one of Europe's liveliest late-night cultures. Its major sights are balanced by great parks, tapas districts and easy day-trip links.

cities.name: Barcelona
cities.summary: Barcelona layers Gaudí architecture, dense old quarters and city beaches into one of Europe's most complete short breaks. It is strong on art, food and street life from morning to late night.

cities.name: Seville
cities.summary: Seville is an atmospheric Andalusian capital of palaces, patios and flamenco. Its compact centre makes it easy to combine major monuments with long evenings of tapas and riverfront walks.

cities.name: Granada
cities.summary: Granada combines the Alhambra with hilltop quarters, tea-house alleys and Sierra Nevada views. It is one of Spain's most rewarding short stays for history and atmosphere.

cities.name: Córdoba
cities.summary: Córdoba is a compact Andalusian gem centred on the Mezquita and flower-filled lanes. One unhurried day covers its major layers of Roman, Islamic and Christian history.

cities.name: Valencia
cities.summary: Valencia balances a lively old centre with futuristic museums, broad beaches and one of Spain's best urban parks. It is a very easy city break with excellent food and family appeal.

clusters.name: Ciutat Vella
attractions: Plaça de la Mare de Déu

clusters.name: Turia Gardens
attractions: Jardí Botànic de la Universitat de València

cities.name: Málaga
cities.summary: Málaga makes a strong short coastal stop with Moorish fortifications, major art museums and an easy beach-front promenade. It is compact, sunny and well connected across Andalusia.

cities.name: Marbella
cities.summary: Marbella combines a pretty old town with beach clubs, marinas and a polished Costa del Sol feel. It is best for sun, dining and a more upscale coastal base.

cities.name: Ronda
cities.summary: Ronda sits dramatically above a deep gorge and packs major views into a walkable hill town. It is ideal for a slow day of scenery, history and white-village atmosphere.

clusters.name: Country Views
attractions: Ermita Rupestre de la Virgen de la Cabeza

cities.name: Bilbao
cities.summary: Bilbao is a food-loving Basque city where bold modern architecture meets a characterful old quarter. It works well for art, pintxos and quick side trips to the coast.

cities.name: San Sebastián
cities.summary: San Sebastián is famed for its elegant bay, compact old town and outstanding pintxos scene. It rewards travellers who want beach time, good walking and top-tier food in one place.

clusters.name: La Concha & Parte Vieja
attractions: Basilica of Saint Mary of the Chorus

cities.name: Toledo
cities.summary: Toledo crowns a river-wrapped hill with one of Spain's richest medieval skylines. It is a dense, high-reward heritage stop with cathedrals, synagogues and superb viewpoints.

clusters.name: Cathedral & Jewish Quarter
attractions: Synagogue of Santa María la Blanca
Monastery of San Juan de los Reyes

clusters.name: Miradors & Gates
attractions: Mezquita del Cristo de la Luz

cities.name: Zaragoza
cities.summary: Zaragoza is an underrated Aragonese city with major basilicas, Roman remains and a broad riverside setting. It fits well as a cultural stop between Madrid, Barcelona and the Basque Country.

clusters.name: Pilar & Ebro
attractions: Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar

cities.name: Ibiza
cities.summary: Ibiza offers more than clubs: walled heritage streets, coves and easy boat days sit alongside famous nightlife. It is best in shoulder season when the sea is warm and the roads are calmer.

cities.name: Mallorca
cities.summary: Mallorca combines Palma's elegant old core with mountain villages, coves and scenic drives. The island easily supports a longer stay split between city sights and beach or hiking days.

clusters.name: Palma Old City
attractions: Cathedral of Santa Maria of Palma

cities.name: Tenerife
cities.summary: Tenerife spans volcanic highlands, resort beaches and laurel-forest walks on one large island. It suits travellers who want warm weather, scenery and varied day trips in any season.

clusters.name: Puerto de la Cruz North
attractions: Botanical Garden of Puerto de la Cruz

cities.name: Gran Canaria
cities.summary: Gran Canaria mixes a city beach, desert-like dunes and a rugged interior of viewpoints and villages. It is one of Europe's easiest islands for all-season sunshine and varied outings.

cities.name: Lisbon
cities.summary: Lisbon spreads across steep hills with miradouros, tiled facades and an excellent food scene. It is one of Europe's best-value capitals for culture, nightlife and easy Atlantic day trips.

cities.name: Sintra
cities.summary: Sintra is Portugal's classic fairy-tale escape, packed with palaces, gardens and misty hilltop views. It merits more than a rushed day trip if you want both monuments and coast.

clusters.name: Pena & Moorish Heights
attractions: Chalet of the Countess of Edla

cities.name: Cascais
cities.summary: Cascais is an easy-going Atlantic resort town with beaches, promenades and a polished marina feel. It works well for a relaxed coastal break or as a Lisbon-side sea escape.

cities.name: Porto
cities.summary: Porto pairs riverfront drama, tiled churches and famous wine lodges with a compact, atmospheric centre. It is highly rewarding for food, views and romantic walks across the Douro.

cities.name: Coimbra
cities.summary: Coimbra is a handsome hill city dominated by Portugal's historic university and student traditions. It is compact, atmospheric and strong on libraries, churches and river views.

cities.name: Faro
cities.summary: Faro combines a walled old town with easy boat access into the lagoons and islands of the Ria Formosa. It is more rewarding than a simple airport stop, especially in shoulder season.

cities.name: Lagos
cities.summary: Lagos is one of the Algarve's best all-round bases, mixing a lively historic centre with famous cliffs and beaches. It suits travellers who want boat trips, swims and easy nightlife.

cities.name: Albufeira
cities.summary: Albufeira is a classic Algarve resort with cliffs, sandy beaches and a big evening scene. It is a practical base for boat trips and beach time, especially for groups and families.

cities.name: Évora
cities.summary: Évora is a beautifully preserved Alentejo city of Roman remains, churches and whitewashed lanes. It makes a rich but manageable heritage stop with strong food and wine nearby.

clusters.name: Roman & Cathedral Core
attractions: Museu Nacional Frei Manuel do Cenáculo

cities.name: Funchal
cities.summary: Funchal is a lush Atlantic island capital backed by steep slopes and famous for gardens, levadas and subtropical produce. It is a strong year-round base for scenery, walking and ocean views.

clusters.name: Monte Heights
attractions: Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Monte

cities.name: Ponta Delgada
cities.summary: Ponta Delgada is the gateway to São Miguel's crater lakes, hot springs and green Atlantic landscapes. It suits travellers who want soft adventure, viewpoints and a slower island rhythm.

clusters.name: Furnas & Hot Springs
attractions: Chapel of Nossa Senhora das Vitórias
